steps.title: Signs: positive or negative?
steps.intro: Multiplication and division share the same sign rules. Addition has its own rules.

tables.title: Add
head: Signs
Result
rows: the sign of the number that is bigger in size: \(-7+3=-4\)

tips: Count only the minus signs: odd count → negative, even count → positive.
Even powers and \(|x|\) are never negative. Odd powers keep the sign: \((-2)^3=-8\).
Bigger minus smaller is positive, even for negative numbers: \(-2-(-5)=3\).
\(-x\) means "the opposite of \(x\)", not "a negative number".
Zero is neither positive nor negative.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} a\ne0 \\ \frac{a^5\cdot b^2}{|a|}<0 \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(b^2\) is an even power, so \(b^2\ge0\). If \(b=0\), the expression equals \(0\), which is not negative. Therefore \(b\ne0\) and \(b^2>0\).
The only piece that can make the expression negative is \(a^5\). An odd power keeps the sign, so \(a^5<0\) means \(a<0\).
Nothing is known about the sign of \(b\). Choice (2) claims too much (\(b<0\) is not necessarily true). Choices (1) and (3) say \(a>0\), which contradicts \(a<0\). The answer is (4).

Method 2 · Mirror test: flip the sign of \(b\) only. \(b\) appears only as \(b^2\), and \((-b)^2=b^2\), so the given stays the same. Choice 2 (\(b<0\)) and choice 3 (\(0<b\)) turn into the opposite about \(b\), so they are out.
Choices 1 and 4 are left. The top, \(a^5\), must be negative, so \(a<0\): choice 4.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} x<0<y \\ x+y>0 \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: x is negative and y is positive: mixed signs. In a sum with mixed signs, the number that is bigger in size wins.
The sum is positive, so the positive number y is bigger in size: \(|y|>|x|\).
The others: (1) is the opposite. (3) Mixed signs give a negative product: \(xy<0\). (4) \(x-y\) is smaller minus bigger, so it is negative.

steps.title: Consecutive integers
steps.intro: Write them with one letter, plug in the smallest legal numbers, or read the differences.
tips: Smaller minus bigger is negative: \(b-a=1\) but \(a-b=-1\).
"Greater than 0" does not mean the list starts at 1.
Plugging in? First check that the choices give different values. If two choices tie, choose other numbers.

steps.stem:
p, q and r are consecutive even numbers, and \(0<p<q<r\)
\(\frac{r^2-p^2}{2q}=?\)
explanation: Write the numbers around the middle: \(p=q-2\) and \(r=q+2\).
The trap is \(2\): it uses a gap of \(1\) (consecutive integers) instead of a gap of \(2\).

steps.stem:
p, q, r and s are consecutive integers, and \(p<q<r<s\)
\(\frac{r-p}{s-r}-\frac{q-s}{r-q}=?\)
explanation: In consecutive integers every difference is a fixed number: \(r-p=2\), \(s-r=1\), \(q-s=-2\), \(r-q=1\).
Watch the signs: \(q-s\) is smaller minus bigger, so it is negative. Subtracting a negative adds. (\(0\) is the trap: it loses that minus.)

steps.stem: The sum of seven consecutive integers is \(91\). What is the largest of them?
explanation: Sum = count × middle, so the middle number is \(\frac{91}{7}=13\).
Seven numbers: three below the middle and three above it: \(10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16\).
The largest is \(13+3=16\). Check: \(7\cdot13=91\) ✓.

steps.stem: The sum of four consecutive integers is always —
explanation: Write the numbers as \(a, a+1, a+2, a+3\). The sum is \(4a+6\).
\(4a+6=2(2a+3)\), so the sum is always even.
\(4a+6=4(a+1)+2\): a multiple of 4, plus 2. So it is never divisible by 4.
Check: \(1+2+3+4=10\) and \(2+3+4+5=14\). Both are even and not divisible by 4. And \(10\) is not divisible by 3, so (4) is out.

steps.title: Sums of consecutive integers
steps.intro: Sum = count × middle. The middle = sum ÷ count.

head: Situation
Rule
Example
rows: the sum is divisible by the count
the sum is never divisible by the count

tips: Four consecutive integers: the sum is \(4a+6\), even but never divisible by 4.

steps.title: Even & odd
steps.intro: Plug in 2 for even and 1 or 3 for odd. For \(\pm\) and \(\times\), one plug-in for each parity case is enough. For division, plug in three times.
tips: In a sum, only the odd terms matter: an odd number of them → odd.
One even factor makes a product even. A product is odd only if every factor is odd.
Powers do not change parity (positive whole exponents).
Division: plug in three times, with numbers close together.
A plug-in can disprove "always", but it cannot prove it.

steps.stem: m and n are positive integers, and \(m+n\) is odd. Which of the following is true about the expression \(m^n+n^m+9+4n\)?
choices: It is odd when \(m\) is odd and \(n\) is even.
It is odd when \(m\) is even and \(n\) is odd.
explanation: Powers do not change parity, so delete them: the expression has the same parity as \(m+n+9+4n\).
\(m+n\) is odd (given), \(9\) is odd, and \(4n\) is even. Odd + odd + even = even.
So the expression is always even. Check: \(m=1\), \(n=2\): \(1^2+2^1+9+8=20\). \(m=2\), \(n=1\): \(2^1+1^2+9+4=16\). Both are even.

steps.stem: a and b are integers. a is odd, and b is even and not \(0\). Which of the following is the most precise description of \(\frac{6a}{b^2}\)?
explanation: b is even, so \(b=2k\) (\(k\) is an integer, \(k\ne0\)). Then \(b^2=4k^2\).
The top, \(3a\), is odd (odd times odd). The bottom, \(2k^2\), is even. Odd divided by even is never an integer, so the result is always a fraction.
The trap is choice (1): "even divided by even can be anything" is true in general, but here the two in b cancels with a two in the six.

steps.stem: a and b are integers. Given: \(a-b=6\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily even?
explanation: \(a-b=6\) is even, so a and b have the same parity: both even or both odd.
Why (2) is always even: \(b^2+ab=b(a+b)\), and \(a+b\) is even, because a and b have the same parity.

steps.title: Special products
steps.intro: These products are ALWAYS divisible by a number, and each rule has a reason. For any other product, the smallest case gives only a candidate.

tables.title: Proven rules
head: Product of…
Why
Always divisible by
rows: one is even, one is divisible by 3
one is divisible by 4, another is even, one is divisible by 3
one of them is divisible by 4

tables.title: The smallest case is only a candidate
head: Product of…
Smallest case
Second case
Always divisible by

tips: Smallest case → cross out the choices that do not divide it. Then test a second case that avoids the factor you are checking.
Integer? Count the twos. \(m\) even, \(n\) odd: \(\frac{m^2(n+1)}{8}\) has three twos on top, so it is always an integer.
Never use a case that gives 0: 0 is divisible by every number, so it tells you nothing.

steps.stem: n is an odd number. Which of the following is the most precise description of \(\frac{9n^2-1}{4}\)?
explanation: \(9n^2-1=(3n-1)(3n+1)\). n is odd, so \(3n\) is odd, and \(3n-1\) and \(3n+1\) are two consecutive even numbers. One of them is divisible by 4, so the product is divisible by 8: \(9n^2-1=8k\).
\(\frac{8k}{4}=2k\), which is always even.
The trap is choice (3): "even divided by even can be anything" — but here the top always has three twos.

steps.stem: n is an integer. The expression \(\frac{n-n^3}{3}\) is always —
explanation: \(n-n^3=n(1-n^2)=-(n-1)\cdot n\cdot(n+1)\): minus a product of three consecutive integers. That product is divisible by 6: \(n-n^3=6k\).
\(\frac{6k}{3}=2k\), which is always even.
Check: \(n=1, 2, 3\) give \(0\), \(-2\), \(-8\). \(-2\) is not divisible by 4, so (1) is out. (A minus sign does not change parity: \(-2\) is even.)

steps.stem: n is a positive odd number. The product \(n(n+2)(n+4)\) is necessarily divisible by —
explanation: Smallest case: \(n=1\) gives \(1\cdot3\cdot5=15\). A number that always divides the product must divide \(15\). \(45\) does not, so (1) is out.
The smallest case is only a candidate. Test a second case with no multiple of 5: \(n=7\) gives \(7\cdot9\cdot11=693\). It ends in 3, so it is not divisible by 5, and not by 15. (2) and (3) are out.
Why 3 always works: every third odd number is a multiple of 3 (\(3, 9, 15, 21, \dots\)). Three odd numbers in a row always include one of them.
Trap: \(n=3\) gives \(105\) and \(n=5\) gives \(315\). Both are divisible by 15, because each product has a 5 inside.

steps.stem: Given: \(w<x<0<y<z\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily negative?
explanation: Bigger minus smaller is positive, and smaller minus bigger is negative. So \(x-w>0\), \(z-y>0\), \(y-z<0\) and \(w-x<0\). Also \(w-z<0\) (negative minus positive), \(x<0\) and \(-y<0\).
Only (1) is necessarily negative. Check with \(w=-2\), \(x=-1\), \(y=1\), \(z=2\): (1) gives \(1\cdot(-1)=-1\).

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} x>y \\ xy<0 \end{cases}\)
Which of the following expressions is necessarily positive?
explanation: \(xy<0\): x and y have opposite signs. Since \(x>y\), the negative one is y: \(y<0<x\).
(1) The top, \(x^2-y\), is positive plus positive, so it is positive. The bottom, \(y\), is negative. Positive divided by negative: negative.
(2) The top, \(y-x\), is smaller minus bigger: negative. The bottom, \(y\), is negative. Negative divided by negative: always positive.
(3) \(\frac{x^2-y^2}{x-y}=\frac{(x-y)(x+y)}{x-y}=x+y\). Mixed signs: the sign depends on which number is bigger in size. Not necessarily positive.
(4) \(\frac{x^2y}{xy^2}=\frac xy\), which is positive divided by negative, so it is negative.
Check with \(x=1\), \(y=-1\): the four choices give \(-2\), \(2\), \(0\), \(-1\). Only (2) is positive.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} p>q \\ p+q+r<0 \end{cases}\)
Which of the following additional givens makes r necessarily negative?
explanation: (4) If \(q>0\), then \(p>q>0\). Both are positive, so \(p+q>0\). For \(p+q+r\) to be negative, r must be negative.
The other choices do not force r to be negative:

steps.stem:
a and b are consecutive even numbers, and c and d are consecutive even numbers. Given:
\(\begin{cases} a<b \\ c<d \\ a+d\ne0 \end{cases}\)
\(\frac{b^2-a^2+d^2-c^2}{a+d}=?\)
explanation: Consecutive even numbers: \(b=a+2\) and \(d=c+2\).
The top: \(4a+4c+8=4(a+c+2)\). The bottom: \(a+d=a+c+2\).
Check with \(a=2\), \(b=4\), \(c=8\), \(d=10\): \(\frac{16-4+100-64}{2+10}=\frac{48}{12}=4\) ✓. (With \(a=c=2\), choices (3) and (4) both give \(4\), so that plug-in cannot decide.)
The trap is \(2\): it uses a gap of \(1\) (consecutive integers) instead of a gap of \(2\).

steps.stem: x, y and z are consecutive integers, and \(x<y<z\). Given: \(x^2+y^2=z^2\). Which of the following could be the value of \(x+z\)?
explanation: Write the numbers around the middle: \(x=y-1\), \(z=y+1\).
\(y=4\): the numbers are \(3, 4, 5\), and \(x+z=3+5=8\). \(y=0\): the numbers are \(-1, 0, 1\), and \(x+z=0\).
Only \(8\) is among the choices. Check: \(9+16=25\) ✓.
Faster: \(x+z=(y-1)+(y+1)=2y\), so the middle is \((x+z)\div2\). For \(8\) the middle is \(4\): \(3^2+4^2=5^2\) ✓.
The trap is \(12\): that is the sum of all three numbers, but the question asks only for \(x+z\).

steps.stem: b and y are integers. Given: \(y=(b-3)^2+(b+8)^3\). Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: \(b-3\) has the opposite parity to b (subtracting an odd number). \(b+8\) has the same parity as b (adding an even number).
Powers do not change parity, so \(y\) has the same parity as \((b-3)+(b+8)=2b+5\), which is always odd.
So y is always odd, and b can be even or odd. Check: \(b=1\) gives \(4+729=733\). \(b=2\) gives \(1+1000=1001\). Both odd.

steps.stem: k, a, b and c are integers. Given: \(2k+1=a^3\cdot(b+1)^2\cdot(c-5)^4\). Which of the numbers k, a, b, c is necessarily odd?
explanation: \(2k+1\) is odd for every integer k. So the product on the right is odd.
A product is odd only if every factor is odd.
\(a^3\) is odd, so a is odd. \((b+1)^2\) is odd, so \(b+1\) is odd and b is even. \((c-5)^4\) is odd, so \(c-5\) is odd and c is even.

steps.stem: a is an odd positive number, and b is an even positive number. Which of the following expressions is not necessarily an integer?
explanation: Count the twos. b is even, so it has at least one two. a is odd, so \(a+1\) and \(a+3\) are even, and \(a+2\) is odd.
(1) \(b^3\) has at least three twos, enough for \(8=2^3\). Always an integer.
(2) \(a+1\) and \(a+3\) are consecutive even numbers, so their product is divisible by 8.
(3) \((a+b)^2+(a-b)^2=2a^2+2b^2\), so the top is \(2b^2\). With \(b=2k\): \(8k^2\). Always divisible by 8.
(4) In \(ab^2\) there are only two twos for sure (a is odd). With \(a=1\) and \(b=2\) the value is \(\frac{1\cdot4}{8}=\frac12\). Not necessarily an integer.
The answer is (4).

steps.stem: a and b are odd integers. Which of the following expressions is necessarily even?
explanation: Why (4) is always even: odd + odd = even.

steps.stem: The sum of three consecutive integers is \(48\). What is the largest of them?
explanation: Sum = count × middle, so the middle number is \(\frac{48}{3}=16\).
The numbers are \(15, 16, 17\). The largest is \(17\).

steps.stem: How many even integers are there between \(-7\) and \(9\)?
explanation: List them: \(-6, -4, -2, 0, 2, 4, 6, 8\). That is 8 numbers. Remember: \(0\) is even.
Or count the steps of two from \(-6\) to \(8\): \(\frac{8-(-6)}{2}+1=7+1=8\).

steps.stem: In a café, every small table has 4 chairs, and every large table has 7 chairs. The number of large tables is odd. The total number of chairs at all the tables is necessarily —
explanation: Total \(=4\cdot(\text{small tables})+7\cdot(\text{large tables})\).
\(4\) times any number is even. \(7\) times an odd number is odd × odd = odd.
Even + odd = odd, so the total is necessarily odd.
Check: 1 small table and 1 large table: \(4+7=11\). Odd, and not divisible by 4 or by 7.

steps.stem: The number \(6^5+5^6\) is —
explanation: \(6^5\) is even. \(5^6\) is odd (an odd number to any power is odd). Even + odd = odd.
An odd number is not divisible by 6. It is not divisible by 5 either: \(5^6\) is divisible by 5, but \(6^5\) is not, so the sum is not.

steps.stem: Given: \(m^6\cdot n^3<0\). Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: \(m^6\) is an even power, so \(m^6\ge0\). If \(m=0\), the product is \(0\), which is not negative. So \(m\ne0\) and \(m^6>0\).
Then \(n^3\) must be negative. An odd power keeps the sign, so \(n<0\).
The sign of m is not known: \(m=1\), \(n=-1\) and \(m=-1\), \(n=-1\) both work.

Method 2 · Mirror test: flip the sign of \(m\) only. \((-m)^6=m^6\), so the given stays the same. Choice 2 (\(m<0\)) turns into \(0<m\), and choice 4 turns into \(m<0\): both turn into their opposites, so they are out.
Choices 1 and 3 are left. \(n^3\) must be negative, so \(n<0\): choice 1.

steps.stem: a and b are odd numbers. Which of the following expressions cannot be an integer?
explanation: a and b are odd, so \(ab\) is odd, and \(\frac a2\cdot b=\frac{ab}{2}\) is an odd number divided by 2. Never an integer.

steps.stem: m and n are integers. Given: \(m-n=8\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily even?
explanation: \(m-n=8\) is even, so m and n have the same parity.
\(m+n\): even + even or odd + odd. Always even.
\(m^2-n^2=(m-n)(m+n)=8(m+n)\). Always even.
\(m^2+n^2\): powers do not change parity, so it has the parity of \(m+n\). Always even.
All three are always even. Check with \(m=9\), \(n=1\): \(10\), \(80\), \(82\).

steps.stem:
x and y are positive consecutive integers, and \(x<y\). Given: \(x^2-y^2=-13\)
\(x+y=?\)
explanation: Consecutive: \(y-x=1\), so \(x-y=-1\) and \(x^2-y^2=(x-y)(x+y)=-(x+y)\).
Shortcut: for consecutive \(x<y\), \(y^2-x^2=x+y\). Check: \(x=6\), \(y=7\): \(36-49=-13\) ✓.

steps.stem:
x, y and z are consecutive positive integers, and \(x<y<z\). Given: \(z^2-x^2=56\)
\(y=?\)
explanation: Consecutive: \(y=x+1\) and \(z=x+2\), so \(z-x=2\) and \(z+x=2x+2\).

steps.stem: Given: \(a<b<c<0\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily positive?
explanation: All three numbers are negative.
(1) \(c<0\) and \(a+b<0\) (negative + negative). Negative × negative = positive, always.
(2) \(a+c<0\) (negative + negative) and \(-b>0\): negative.
(3) \(bc>0\), divided by \(a<0\): negative.
(4) \((-a)(-c)>0\), times \(b<0\): negative. The answer is (1).

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} a+b<0 \\ ab>0 \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: \(a<0\), but the sign of \(b\) cannot be determined
explanation: \(ab>0\): a and b have the same sign, and neither of them is \(0\).
If both were positive, the sum would be positive. The sum is negative, so both are negative.

steps.stem:
a, b and c are consecutive integers, and \(a<b<c\). Given: \(a^2+c^2=20b-48\)
\(a+b+c=?\)
explanation: Write the numbers around the middle: \(a=b-1\), \(c=b+1\).
The numbers are \(4, 5, 6\), and the sum is \(3b=15\). Check: \(16+36=52\) and \(20\cdot5-48=52\) ✓.
Or test the choices: the middle is the sum divided by 3. \(18\): middle \(6\), \(25+49=74\ne72\). \(12\): middle \(4\), \(9+25=34\ne32\). \(5\) is not divisible by 3.

steps.stem:
a, b and c are consecutive integers, and \(0<a<b<c\). The product of the three numbers is 16 times their sum.
\(b=?\)
explanation: Write the numbers around the middle: \(a=b-1\), \(c=b+1\). The sum is \(3b\) (count × middle). The product is \((b-1)b(b+1)\).

steps.stem: a and b are prime numbers, and \(a\le b\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily even?
explanation: If \(b=2\), then \(a\le2\) forces \(a=2\): \(a(b+3)=2\cdot5=10\), even.
If b is an odd prime, \(b+3\) is even, so \(a(b+3)\) is even.

steps.stem: n is an even number. Which of the following could be the value of \(\frac{n^3}{2}\)?
explanation: n is even: \(n=2k\). Then \(n^3=8k^3\), so \(\frac{n^3}{2}=4k^3\). It must be divisible by 4.
Only \(108\) is divisible by 4 (\(74\), \(62\) and \(90\) are not). And \(108\) works: \(n^3=216\), so \(n=6\) ✓.

steps.stem: t and k are integers. Given: \(2k+1=t(6t+5)\). t is necessarily —
explanation: \(2k+1\) is odd for every integer k. \(6t+5\) is also odd, because \(6t\) is even.
A product is odd only if every factor is odd. So t is odd.
Divisibility by 3 is not fixed: \(t=1\) gives \(1\cdot11=11=2\cdot5+1\) (\(k=5\)), and \(t=3\) gives \(3\cdot23=69=2\cdot34+1\) (\(k=34\)).

steps.stem: m and n are consecutive integers. Given: \(x=m^2-n^2+5n-5m\). Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: m and n are consecutive: \(m-n=1\) or \(m-n=-1\). Also \(m+n\) is odd (one even, one odd), so \(m+n-5\) is odd − odd = even.
So \(x=(\pm1)\cdot(\text{even})\), and x is always even.
The sign is not fixed: \(m=1\), \(n=2\) gives \(x=(-1)\cdot(-2)=2\). \(m=2\), \(n=1\) gives \(x=1\cdot(-2)=-2\).

steps.stem: a and b are integers. The expression \((a-1)(6b+a)\) is necessarily —
explanation: \(6b\) is even, so \(6b+a\) has the same parity as a. \(a-1\) has the opposite parity. So one of the two factors is even, and the product is always even.

The others fail: (1) With \(a=1\) the product is \(0\). (2) With \(a=-3\) and \(b=1\) the product is \((-4)\cdot3=-12\), negative. (3) With \(a=5\) and \(b=1\) the product is \(4\cdot11=44\), not divisible by 5.

steps.stem: Which of the following could be the sum of four consecutive integers?
explanation: The sum of \(a, a+1, a+2, a+3\) is \(4a+6=4(a+1)+2\): even, but never divisible by 4.
\(20\), \(24\) and \(28\) are divisible by 4, so they are out.

steps.stem: n is a positive integer. The product \((n+1)(n+2)(n+3)\) is necessarily divisible by —
explanation: Three consecutive integers: the product is always divisible by 6 (one of them is even, and one is divisible by 3).
The smallest case, \(n=1\), gives \(2\cdot3\cdot4=24\). All four choices divide 24, so it only gives candidates.
Second case: \(n=2\) gives \(3\cdot4\cdot5=60\). \(24\) and \(8\) do not divide 60. Out.
A case with no multiple of 4: \(n=4\) gives \(5\cdot6\cdot7=210\). \(12\) does not divide 210. Out. The answer is \(6\).

steps.stem:
a and b are positive integers, and \(a<b\). Given:
\(\begin{cases} ab^2\text{ is even} \\ a+b\text{ is odd} \end{cases}\)
Which of the following statements is not correct?
explanation: \(a+b\) is odd, so one of a and b is even and the other is odd.
\(a^2b\) contains the even one, so it is even. The statement "\(a^2b\) is odd" is not correct.
The others are correct: (1) \(b^2+b=b(b+1)\) is a product of consecutive numbers, so it is even. (3) \(a+b-1=\text{odd}-1=\text{even}\). (4) Even minus odd, or odd minus even, is odd.

steps.stem: n is an integer greater than 1. At least half of the integers from 2 to n (inclusive) are —
explanation: The list starts with 2, which is even, and then goes even, odd, even, odd. So there are never fewer even numbers than odd numbers.
For \(n=5\): \(2, 3, 4, 5\), and \(2, 4\) are even (2 of 4, exactly half). For \(n=6\): \(2, 4, 6\) are even (3 of 5, more than half).

The others fail: (1) For \(n=3\), both \(2\) and \(3\) are prime (0 of 2 not prime). (3) For \(n=4\), only \(3\) is odd (1 of 3). (4) For \(n=10\), the primes are \(2, 3, 5, 7\) (4 of 9, less than half).

steps.stem: a and b are positive integers. Given: \(ab=100\). Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
choices: if a is \(\text{odd}\) then b is \(\text{even}\)
if b is \(\text{even}\) then a is \(\text{odd}\)
explanation: \(100=2^2\cdot5^2\). If a is odd, a has no factor 2, so both twos are in b. Then b is even. So (1) is always true.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} x>y \\ xy<z \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is not possible?
explanation: If \(x<0\), then \(y<x<0\). Both are negative, so \(xy>0\).
If also \(z<0\), then \(xy<z\) says that a positive number is less than a negative number. Impossible. So (3) is not possible.

steps.stem: a and b are positive integers. a is odd and b is even. Which of the following expressions is necessarily an integer?
explanation: Count the twos. a is odd, so \(a-1\) and \(a+1\) are consecutive even numbers: one is divisible by 2 and the other by 4. That is three twos. b is even: one more two. Four twos: \(2^4=16\). So (3) is always an integer.
